THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:14719  CRL.P No. 103197 of 2023  ORDER Heard Sri Chetan T.Limbikai, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Praveena Y.
Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 and Sri Veeresh S.Gadad, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

The petitioner is seeking regular bail in Crime No.33/2023 of Sirsi Town Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(f) of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") Sections 4, 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

3. Brief facts of the case:-
It is the case of the complaint that the complainant is the victim, aged about 16 years 8 months as on the date of the alleged incident.
She was studying in I PUC (Commerce) and was staying at her maternal aunt's house.
The petitioner being the uncle's son used to going to the house of her maternal aunt.
The victim was informed that the petitioner was loving her.
The marriage of the petitioner was solemnized with another woman.

Even though,
the petitioner was insisting her that he would marry her.
It is further alleged that on the NC: 2023:KHC-D:14719 pretext of marriage, the petitioner said to have committed sexual assault on several occasions.
Consequently, she became pregnant.
The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment, where the Doctor has diagnosed that she is pregnant.
The case came to be registered against the petitioner on 26.04.2023.
The victim was produced before of the Magistrate to record her statement.
The victim has not supported in the statement made before the Magistrate.
However, the jurisdictional police have filed a charge sheet.
4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offences.
He has been falsely implicated in this case.
The victim has not supported the case in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
The petitioner is a permanent resident of Aladakatti village, Haveri taluk and is having a wife and children and he has to take care of his aged parents.
If the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.

Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays Sri Mohammad Aspak Chouti vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142230940/
2 to allow the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, Shri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara, the learned HCGP vehemently opposed the bail application and submits that the offences alleged are committed against the minor, which is heinous in nature and she became pregnant.
The petitioner and others have threatened her to give statement before the Magistrate in such a manner.
Therefore, it is not appropriate to grant bail.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss petition.
6. On other hand, Sri. Veeresh S.Gadad, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 adopted the submission of the learned High Court Government Pleader and prays to reject the petition.
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties, and perused the averments of the charge sheet and also complaint, it appears that the petitioner herein was loving the victim.
The victim was studying in I PUC and staying in her maternal aunt's house.
The petitioner on the pretext of marriage has committed sexual assault against the victim on several occasions.

On 15.10.2022,
when the victim was sleeping in the bed room in the house of her maternal aunt, the NC:
2023:KHC-D:14719 petitioner said to have committed sexual assault.
Thereafter, she was diagnosed as pregnant.
Immediately, complaint came to be registered against the petitioner.
However, in the statement recorded by the Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, the victim has turned hostile.
When the averments of the complaint and statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. is inconsistent, it is not appropriate to keep the petitioner in judicial custody for longer period.

Therefore, considering the avocation and the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. of the victim,
the petition is deserved to be allowed.

8. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.33/2023 of Sirsi Town Police Station on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:14719 a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
